research.thesis: Ethereum's 18.3% surge to $2,291.78—backed by $2.32B in Binance spot volume—was catalyzed by a historic $3B+ market-wide short squeeze, shifting price structure from range-bound compression to violent expansion.
research.strongest_signal: ETHUSDT broke out from $1,932.79 to an intraday high of $2,333.65 on Binance with $2.32B in 24-hour spot volume, coinciding with over $3B in total short liquidations across the market.

draft.title: The Anatomy of a $3B Squeeze: How ETH Surged 18% to $2,291
draft.post:
More than $3 billion in short positions were wiped out across the crypto market in a single day, driving Ethereum through a massive 18.3% breakout on $2.32 billion in Binance spot volume.

According to Binance spot market data, ETH open prices moved from an intraday low of $1,932.79, slicing through key technical levels to touch a high of $2,333.65 before settling into consolidation around $2,291.78.

The initial leg up was triggered by heavy volume spikes—over 195,000 ETH traded on Binance during the first hourly candle breaking $2,100. As prices accelerated, crowded derivative shorts were forced to buy back into thin order books, accelerating the upward momentum.

Reports from CoinDesk highlighted the extreme velocity of the unwind, including a single trader losing $24 million on an ETH short position in just 12 seconds during the surge.

What matters now is market structure. Following the liquidation cascade, ETH has established a tight consolidation band between $2,240 and $2,290. When a rally is driven by forced short-covering, holding these newly reclaimed levels requires spot buyers to absorb secondary profit-taking.

Do you see this breakout holding above $2,250, or are we looking at a temporary leverage flush before a range retest?
